images.title: Up from below ground
images.purpose: Show that going from −200 m to +2000 m needs +200 to reach zero and then +2000 more, so +2200.
images.composition: One tall vertical line centred with two stacked arrows and the ground line in the middle, plenty of white space.
images.exact_structure: One vertical line with a grey #6B7280 ground line at 0 in the middle. A teal #0072B2 dot below it at −200 and an amber #E69F00 dot above it at +2000. A short reddish purple #CC79A7 upward arrow from −200 to 0, and a long amber upward arrow from 0 to +2000, the long one clearly bigger. Exactly 3 marked levels, 2 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the two arrows drawn the same length
images.takeaway: Up from below ground is the climb to zero plus the climb above it.
images.description: A vertical line with a dot at −200, the ground at 0 and a dot at +2000; a short arrow of +200 to zero and a long arrow of +2000 more, total +2200.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the two arrows and add their sizes.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
